1010.t: Gulf Coast string outfit and the original Owls personnel
1010.s: The instruments and members of the summer hotel group, then the five original Owls and later additions at the Roosevelt.
1010.q: We had, it was a funny thing, we had a banjo, a guitar, two violins, and Guy Lyman on this contraption he had, it wasn't a drum, it was just a box with a bunch of plates on it that he would beat on.

621.s: He describes seven-piece combinations, banjo versus guitar, no tuba, violin doubling, and being the only non-reader, taught by Piron.
621.q: when did they use them separately? Well, they didn't have, no, the orchestra I, I, I was with, never did use no guitar. They started off with banjo. Banjo was the first instrument to take out.

763.t: Why he dropped guitar and instrumentation of early bands
763.s: Guitar could not be heard with brass, banjos came in, and bands had trumpet, clarinet, trombone, bass and drums with no piano.
763.ch: Playing bass in the early bands
763.q: Well, you see, that's what made me drop the guitar because I couldn't make a living on it. The only thing I could do is just, like I say, to play for the Mexicans for their singings, for their serenades, I'd make a few dollars. But it was not in demand. See, because at that time there was no such…

126.t: Members and instruments of the Six and Seven Eighths
126.s: Hardy names the seven members, their instruments, and explains the name came from the short violinist Harrison.
126.q: The first group that we had was composed of Dr. Edmond Souchon and Bob and Harry Reynolds and Shields O'Ranagan and Bernie Shields and Harrison, Midget Harrison and Roland Rorschach.

272.t: Ringside instrumentation: banjo, jazz violin, saxes and a Chicago pianist
272.s: Photo details: Angelo played banjo like a pianist, Oscar played melody on violin, no trumpet, and a Chicago pianist was a fine accompanist.
272.ch: Ringside orchestra and New Orleans players
272.q: He didn't play no guitar or nothing in heaven like that. He used it rather. In other words, that boy would sit down and play a single note or anything. Play a melody, play anything you want. Just like a piano player.

629.t: Old band instruments, violins and Tiger Rag
629.s: They discuss absent saxophones, melophone, sousaphone, violins as lead, and Tiger Rag.
629.q: Now, what kind of a part did the violin play? Something like the clarinet or the lead? No, the lead. They always played just the straight balloting? The lead. The lead. Yes. Did you like working with a violin in a band? Yes, it did. That's why it's so little. A band. For what I think played. Yes. I…

923.t: Photo of Tom with Chink Martin, Steve Loyacano and a New Orleans band
923.s: Identifying the band members in a photo and describing their mutes, banjo, violin and doubling saxophones.
923.ch: New Orleans bands and later photographs
923.q: They used to double, I guess. Mm-hmm.

713.t: What bands his uncle played in and his instruments
713.s: Nelson says his uncle played with Punch, Sam Morgan and Guy Kelly, switching between banjo, guitar, trombone and alto horn, and preferred guitar; he never learned electric guitar.
713.ch: Down in St. Bernard and the uncle
713.q: only thing he used to tell me he would go out and play with Punch mm-hmm cause I don't remember when Punch came and I think he came from Racely yeah him and my uncle was together yeah he played with Grenier Sam Morgan I know that he told me once he was playing with Guy Kelly I don't know something…

287.t: Brass band versus string band: Tuxedo, Olympia, Imperial
287.s: Bands such as the Tuxedo (Celestin) had a brass band and a string band. Players doubled, the tuba on string bass, and strings meant banjo and guitar.
287.ch: Brass bands, funerals and working conditions
287.q: No, they, they add on to the marching band. It's like the, kind of time, the bass, the tuba player would double on string bass. And they'd use the Sam, uh, Celestan always had another trumpet with him. He used two trumpets. Sam trombone.

635.t: No tubas in the old bands; the Red Light job
635.s: There were no tubas in bands until about 1920-21. The Magnolia Band worked nightly in the Red Light district at Huntz and Nagel's.
635.q: Well there were no tubas in old bands back in them days. The tubas didn't come in the bands until around the 20s, 20s or 21. Then they started making tubas for the bands. So where did the Magnolia Band play? See we worked every night in the Red Electric District. After we were taking them. See the…

688.t: What a string band was, and Piron's band
688.s: He explains why bands with piano, guitar, bass and violin were called string bands, citing Piron.
688.q: Why they call it a string band? That drum, piano, guitar and bass. So this, that trumpet and trombone was the only two, you know what I mean, in sight. The rest was all string instruments. So they used to call it a string band. And violin? Yeah, they used to use violin too. See like Piron? Yeah.…

290.t: Personnel and instrumentation of the Superior band
290.s: Players in Billy Moreira's Superior band, and use of guitars, banjos, pianos, violins and string bass in early small bands.
290.ch: Youth, Storyville and the bands he heard
290.q: Yeah, well I don't know, but Buddy and Yannick, poor for some one player. Yeah. Yeah. And Walter Brundy, I think you used. Walter Brundy was a drummer. Yeah. He worked with Roebeshaw for a long, long time. All the time I knew him used to work with John Roebeshaw.

54.t: The early six-piece string band with Bud
54.s: The band had two guitars, mandolins, violin and voice, six players; McAllister was with Bud for forty-three years.
54.ch: Bud Scott band instrumentation and repertoire
54.q: Just the guitar, just the playing string guitar. Not the, just the playing the old six strings. No, I'm talking a band is what I mean. Well, we had, uh, two guitars and voice. Three malons and a, two malons and a violin. Six of us, I think. Yeah, just six. Was that violin? Two guitars, yes, that…

195.t: Bill Boyd's band: playing the blues, instrumentation and records
195.s: Crowds waited for the solo choruses on St. Louis Blues, and tunes were played twice in a row. The band had two guitars, bass, two violins, banjo and piano, and Parker recorded with Boyd later, after joining the Doughboys.
195.q: Well, that was the band that was playing there, and they liked all the, oh, that's what they mainly liked, and whenever we'd play old St. Louis blues and some little old dive there, and I'd take three or four courses, people would come around there, they'd stand around, you see, and they would stop…

56.t: Buying real instruments and the band members
56.s: With picnic money he bought valve trombone, violin, twelve-string guitar, bass, trumpet and drum and named the players.
56.q: Well, I bought a valve trombone, violin, twelve-string guitar. Twelve-string guitar? Yeah. With six double strings? Yeah.

833.t: The Forest River Band: a string band with no clarinet or piano
833.s: He describes his small band of cornet, violin, two guitars and bass violin, with no trombone, piano or clarinet.
833.q: Yeah, only, yeah. Only him. I took lessons from him. Only him. Now, the name of the little band was Forest River Band, you know? Forest River Band. Of course, River. That was the name of your band? Yeah, band, yeah. We had six pieces, I think. Two guitar, bass violin, cornet, and violin. That makes…

667.t: Leaving Ventura, marriage and the amplified cello group
667.s: After Ventura they marry and form a group with cello, guitar and bass that audiences are not ready for.
667.ch: Cello group, family and the road
667.q: I think part of the reason too is the fact that we started it and we weren’t that famous yet. I mean we had gotten a certain amount of notoriety with Charlie with the records, and we had a certain following, but we weren’t that well known. And when we first started with this group, we were working…

641.s: The band had banjo, tenor sax, trombone, trumpet (Dimes, Buddy Petit), clarinet, drums and sometimes string bass; no guitars.
641.ch: Clarinet teachers and the Baton Rouge scene
641.q: ...trombone player named Tram... He had different trumpet players. He had a real good trumpet player from New Orleans named Dimes.

74.t: No one set the band's style; Haymen's violin; the Plaza photograph
74.s: The style came from the whole group; Wendell Haymen played violin, and a photograph from the Plaza in 1927 is described.
74.ch: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
74.q: That's right, he was the violin player. I forgot about that.

13.t: When tuba faded and Hines's 1931 strings band
13.s: The first band had two clarinets, two fiddles and cello, giving a chamber sound.
13.q: I don't remember. It just -- tuba just started fading out, with all the big bands, just started fading out tuba, and the bass player was just playing string bass.
